subject: Observability delivery for NexusBank private deploy — telemetry consumers, scrubbing, and trace hooks
body:
From: security@nexusbank.com
To: evelyn_hart@redwood.ai; kimberly_park@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 1 Dec 2026 10:08:00 -0800
Subject: Telemetry delivery constraints for private deployment

Hi Evelyn / Kimberly,

Thanks for the call earlier — following up with the specifics the security team needs to sign off on Redwood's observability plan for our on-prem deployment. Primary asks:
- Minimal outbound ports (we prefer a single TLS egress to a hardened collector).
- Must be able to show data flows for logs, metrics, and traces separately (retention & residency controls).
- PII/redaction at source: we need a recommended scrub pipeline and verification steps.
- SIEM integration: Splunk HEC is our canonical ingest, but we might need an alternate syslog sink for airgapped segments.

Can you send a short design that covers buffering/backpressure, auth (mTLS vs token), and trace header propagation (B3/x-b3 vs W3C)?

Security, NexusBank

---

On Tue, 1 Dec 2026 at 13:20, evelyn_hart@redwood.ai wrote:
To: security@nexusbank.com; ops@nexusbank.com; kimberly_park@redwood.ai; diego_fernandez@redwood.ai
Subject: Re: Telemetry delivery constraints for private deployment

Hi team — thanks for the clear asks. Attaching a concise pattern doc (telemetry_schema_v1.csv) and a sketch of the trace hook (onprem-tracehook-diagram.png). High level notes below.

1) Egress consolidation
- We recommend a single outbound TLS endpoint per VPC segment: an aggregated collector (customer-managed) that you host in a DMZ or bastion subnet. That collector proxies through a narrow set of IPs/ports to Redwood's forwarder when needed.
- For fully air-gapped zones we support a pull model (S3-compatible buffer from the forwarder) and a signed-bundle transfer process for audits.

2) Authentication and authorization
- Prefer mTLS (mutual TLS) for persistent collector-to-forwarder links. Token-based HEC is supported for short-lived flows (e.g., Splunk HEC with rotating tokens).
- We include per-route RBAC in the forwarder so you can restrict which systems push metrics vs logs vs traces.

3) Scrubbing and sampling
- Redaction should happen as close to the source as possible. We support configurable scrub rules in the forwarder (regex, JSON-path, pii-categories).
- We recommend two-layer verification: (a) unit tests in your integrator pipeline against a canonical prompt set, and (b) a small sample of post-scrub payloads delivered to an isolated audit index in Splunk for validation.

4) SIEM (Splunk) integration patterns
- Preferred: Splunk HEC over TLS with batching and ack-based backpressure.
- Alternate: RFC5424 syslog over TLS to a log aggregator for networks that cannot reach HEC.
- For trace-linkage we attach trace_id as a top-level field in log events (B3/x-b3 or W3C traceparent supported).

5) Tracing hooks
- We support OpenTelemetry exporters. Default: W3C traceparent propagation for cross-service compatibility. If you require B3 we can enable an adapter that maps headers and preserves span context.
- Sampling: head-based 1% default for customer-level traces; adjustable per-service with local override.

6) Reliability and backlog handling
- On-host forwarder uses a bounded disk buffer with configurable retention (default 48h). When the network is congested we perform exponential backoff and per-route priority to avoid telemetry storming the link.
- For longer outages we provide signed chunk bundles (AES-256 encrypted) that can be pulled by Redwood on-demand and validated with a checksum.

Next steps: Kimberly and Diego — can you review the attached schema and the tracehook sketch and flag any gaps by end of day Thursday? We'll prepare a short SOW appendix for the compliance team.

Thanks,
Evelyn Hart
Director, Product — Observability
Redwood Inference

---

On Wed, 2 Dec 2026 at 09:04, kimberly_park@redwood.ai wrote:
To: evelyn_hart@redwood.ai; security@nexusbank.com; diego_fernandez@redwood.ai; jonas_weber@redwood.ai
Subject: Re: Telemetry delivery constraints for private deployment

Adding a few specifics from engineering feasibility review:

- Port consolidation: We'll ask Nexus to allow outbound 443 to a specific CIDR (we'll provide minimal set). If you cannot open outbound from certain enclaves, we will configure an on-prem relay that writes encrypted bundles to an S3-compatible endpoint (customer-controlled).
- Scrubbing: Known limitation — pattern-based redaction cannot guarantee 100% for free-form text fields. For high-risk fields (PII), recommend schema enforcement at source (application telemetry library) to avoid accidental capture.
- Splunk HEC: We support ack-based delivery. For very high throughput ingestion (multi-GB/min), we recommend an internal indexer pool before HEC to smooth bursts.
- Sampling & correlation: We'll include an optional sidecar that enforces sampling rules and appends service metadata to traces and logs for deterministic correlation.

I've attached a checklist we can include in the SOW appendix: items for network, retention, audit, and verification.

Kimberly Park
Sr. Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

Attachment: telemetry_schema_v1.csv

---

On Thu, 3 Dec 2026 at 11:15, ops@nexusbank.com wrote:
To: evelyn_hart@redwood.ai; kimberly_park@redwood.ai; diego_fernandez@redwood.ai
Cc: security@nexusbank.com
Subject: Re: Telemetry delivery constraints for private deployment

Appreciate the details. A few clarifying Qs from our infra team:
1) Can you provide the exact header names you will look for when correlating traces to logs? (we want to add them to our ingress gateway)
2) How do you surface evidence of scrubbing (we need tamper-evident proof for audit)?
3) For the bundle pull model, what auth methods do you accept?

Also — are you able to do a dry-run with our staging Splunk next week? We can provision a test HEC with limited retention.

Ops, NexusBank

---

On Thu, 3 Dec 2026 at 16:42, diego_fernandez@redwood.ai wrote:
To: ops@nexusbank.com; evelyn_hart@redwood.ai; kimberly_park@redwood.ai; jonas_weber@redwood.ai
Subject: Re: Telemetry delivery constraints for private deployment

Thanks — answers inline.

1) Trace headers we correlate on:
- Primary: W3C traceparent (traceparent header).
- Back-compat: X-B3-TraceId, X-B3-SpanId, X-B3-Sampled (we will accept and map these to the internal W3C model).
- In logs we add a "trace_id" and "span_id" top-level attribute for tooling convenience.

2) Evidence of scrubbing:
- Each scrub pipeline run emits a signed manifest (SHA-256) listing files processed, number of redactions by rule, and a short sample of redacted vs original hash (we only keep hashes of originals).
- Manifests are timestamped and signed with an HSM-backed key (we can use customer KMS or Redwood-managed per contract). That manifest is stored in an audit bucket (customer-owned) and can be pulled during audits.

3) Bundle pull auth methods:
- Preferred: mutual TLS with client certificate pinned to a CN naming convention.
- Alternate: pre-signed short-lived URL (signed with customer KMS) or SFTP with key-based auth.

Dry-run: yes — we can do a staged integration with your Splunk HEC. Kimberly and Jonas, please coordinate dates; ops, send us an initial set of sample events and a staging HEC endpoint.

Diego Fernandez
Principal Engineer, Observability
Redwood Inference
